title: Intensive group treatment for children with selective mutism
summary: Selective mutism is an anxiety disorder in which those affected do not speak in certain social situations, even though they are able to speak in other situations. This study investigates whether intensive group treatment can help children with selective mutism speak more frequently in various social situations. Children aged five to nine years will participate in the study. The treatment consistes parent training, a preparatory week, and a five-day intensive group treatment. Symptoms will be assessed twice before treatment, immediately after treatment, again approximately three months later and again approximately one year later.  Parent questionnaires and interviews with parents will be used for this purpose.

interventions.name: The study and intensive group treatment will be advertised via social media and support groups, as well as in outpatient clinics for clinical child and adolescent psychology. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Children aged four to ten years with selective mutism as primary diagnosis will be included. Parents have to complete an initial consultation, receive information about the study procedures, intervention, and requirements, and provide informed consent for participation. The child and at least one parent must have sufficient knowledge of German. Participants will be also selected based on age in order to obtain a relatively homogeneous age distribution within the groups.
Exclusion criteria:
Children who do not meet the inclusion criteria will be excluded.
